newsitem.title: USA: Get Trie back from China, congressman tells Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Get Trie back from China, congressman tells Clinton.

text.p: A senior Republican on Tuesday asked President Bill Clinton to find out whether a friend and former contributor had fled to China, saying he should be returned before consideration begins on extending Beijing's favourable trading status.

Rules committee chairman Gerald Solomon, a New York Republican, wrote in a letter to Clinton that he should direct Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to determine the whereabouts of Charles Yah Lin Trie.

Trie, a Little Rock restaurant owner and longtime friend of Clinton, delivered $640,000 to Clinton's legal defence fund, set up to help the president pay for representation in various investigations. The money was returned after its source could not be determined.
Two congressional committees and the Justice Department would like to interview Trie about his fund-raising activities, but he has disappeared and is believed to be in Beijing.
"If Mr. Trie is indeed in China, it is vital that he be returned before any renewal of Most Favoured Nation status even be considered," Solomon wrote to Clinton.
"That is not to say that the return of Mr. Trie would convince me and a number of other members that renewing China's MFN is advisable, considering that nation's performance in other areas," he said.
Solomon said China could easily force Trie to return to the United States if it wanted to. Failure to do so would raise even more questions about its intentions, he said.

Clinton must decide by early June whether to renew China's MFN status, which is accorded to all but a few U.S. trading partners. Opposition is growing among some conservative Republicans who object to China's human rights record and its attitude towards Taiwan as well as allegations that Beijing may have tried to buy influence in U.S. elections.
They are also disturbed by the possibility of Beijing restricting political rights in Hong Kong after it takes over in July.
